name: How much does it cost to hire a failure-to-diagnose lawyer?

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to hire a failure-to-diagnose lawyer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most medical malpractice lawyers work on a contingency fee basis. This means you do not pay upfront legal fees. Instead, the lawyer's payment is a percentage of the compensation recovered in your case, whether through a settlement or a court award. If no compensation is recovered, you generally owe no attorney fees. You may still be responsible for case-related expenses, such as court filing fees or expert witness costs, regardless of the outcome.
acceptedAnswer.description: Many failure-to-diagnose lawyers work on contingency, meaning you pay no upfront fees; their payment is a percentage of your recovery.
